sections.section_title: Pharmacology and Pathophysiology: GLP-1 Agonists and Muscle Toxicity
sections.description: This section provides the necessary background on GLP-1 receptor agonists and the spectrum of muscle-related adverse events, establishing the context for understanding the case report. It explains the mechanisms of action, known side effects, and the pathophysiology of immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM) to prepare the reader for the diagnostic challenge.
subtopics: Mechanism of action of GLP-1 receptor agonists in metabolic disease
Spectrum of musculoskeletal adverse effects: muscle mass loss versus rhabdomyolysis
Overview of Immune-Mediated Necrotising Myopathy (IMNM) and hallmark autoantibodies
Historical context of statin-associated autoimmune myopathy and HMGCR antibodies
Potential mechanisms for drug-induced autoimmune reactions

sections.section_title: Clinical Manifestations: Identifying Immune-Mediated Necrotising Myopathy
sections.description: This section details the clinical presentation of the patient, focusing on the timeline of symptoms and physical examination findings. It teaches the reader how to distinguish between acute drug intolerance, deconditioning, and progressive autoimmune myopathy based on symptom clusters and progression.
subtopics: Timeline analysis: Acute gastrointestinal reaction versus delayed muscle weakness
Clinical hallmarks of proximal myopathy (weakness, dysphagia, dysphonia)
Differentiating deconditioning from pathological muscle weakness
Recognition of bulbar involvement as a critical red flag
Physical examination findings specific to severe proximal weakness

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: Workup and Histopathological Confirmation
sections.description: This section guides the reader through the diagnostic workup, explaining the interpretation of laboratory values, imaging, and biopsy results. It emphasizes the reasoning process used to rule out alternative diagnoses and confirm IMNM, particularly in seronegative cases.
subtopics: Laboratory interpretation: CK elevation patterns and distinguishing hepatic versus muscle enzyme sources
Utility of myositis autoantibody panels and significance of seronegative results
MRI findings in necrotising myopathy (muscle edema distribution and subcutaneous involvement)
Histopathological criteria for IMNM: necrosis, myophagocytosis, and MAC deposition
Differential diagnosis: Toxic myopathy versus autoimmune myopathy versus polymyositis

sections.description: This section outlines the treatment protocol used in the case, providing a framework for managing drug-induced IMNM. It covers the rationale for specific immunosuppressive agents, dosing strategies, and monitoring parameters to ensure safety and efficacy.
subtopics: Indications for immunosuppression in drug-induced IMNM
Protocol for pulse corticosteroids and subsequent oral tapering
Role of IVIG in severe or refractory cases of myopathy
Monitoring therapeutic response via CK trends and functional status
Safety considerations and strategies for weaning off immunosuppression

sections.section_title: Clinical Implications: Causality Assessment and Pharmacovigilance
sections.description: This final section synthesizes the case to discuss the broader clinical significance. It teaches the reader how to assess drug causality using standardized criteria and highlights the importance of pharmacovigilance for emerging medication classes like GLP-1 agonists.
subtopics: Applying WHO-UMC causality criteria to adverse drug reactions
Distinguishing direct toxicity from drug-induced autoimmunity based on clinical course
Importance of pharmacovigilance for emerging medication classes
Clinical recommendations for monitoring patients on GLP-1 agonists
Ethical considerations regarding rechallenge in severe adverse events
